newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 stages rebound before senate elections.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 stages rebound before senate elections.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index posted its first gain in seven sessions on Friday as voters started going to the polls in the country's first Senate elections.
Major issues rose strongly led by Komercni Banka, which rose 99 crown to 2,038. SPT Telecom gained 50 crowns to 2,755 and Ceska Sporitelna moved nine crowns higher to 296.

Power utility CEZ, long the worst performer amongst the heavily capitalised shares, rose by 15 crowns to 937 after posting nine month net profits of 8.4 billion crowns versus 7.4 billion in the same period in 1995.
"CEZ is undervalued as concerns fundamentals but market sentiment is not very strong. The CEZ results were slightly better than I expected," said Petr Douska of Zivnostenska Banka.
"I don't expect the price to go up to 1,000 crowns in the next few days," he added.
Elsewhere in the market, broader issues were almost evenly balanced between advancers and decliners.

British brewer Bass's Czech unit Prazske Pivovary was one of the bigger gainers. It rose 111 crowns to 2,334. North Moravian brewery Radegast, 20 percent owned by Bass, also rose, by 50 crowns to 4,850.
Turnover was thin at 519 million crowns.
